notes:
Summary: Procurement-stage negotiation focused on hard throughput guarantees for Dedicated capacity. Aequitas runs high-volume financial QA and real-time customer chat; cannot tolerate sustained backpressure during market spikes. They want reserved capacity with contractual minimums and predictable burst behavior.

Key throughput asks (customer language / paraphrase):
- "We need a guaranteed floor: 45k tokens/sec sustained for core chat pipeline across the reserved pool, with headroom for bursts."
- Concurrency cap requirement: 250 concurrent active sessions with median P99 latency < 120ms for token streaming.
- Burst policy: allow 3x token-rate bursts for up to 60s with automatic graceful throttling fallback (not outright queueing) and a fallback model that preserves functionality.

Reserved GPU planning notes:
- Proposal: 12 x H100-class GPUs dedicated (estimated based on our perf tests) with autoscale burst pool of additional 4 GPUs for short spikes. Customer asked for mapping to tokens/sec numbers and an explicit failover runbook.
- They want quantization and batching profiles pre-approved to reduce unit cost; require performance verification on their test corpus.

SLA / SLO negotiation points:
- Minimum contractual metric: min_tokens_per_second for pool (customer insisted on an absolute number). Redwood must supply measurement method, reporting cadence, and credit formula for breaches.
- Latency SLO: P99 per-token time target for streaming responses; they want 120ms P99 or credits.
- Concurrency: define per-customer/session concurrency caps and overage behavior; customer wants hard cap of 250 but soft-burst to 750 for <=60s.
- Availability SLA: 99.95% for dedicated pool, but they requested a 99.99% option (enterprise add-on).

Recent timeline / activity (bulleted):
- 2026-01-15: Lead created from stealth performance booth at FinInfra conf.
- 2026-01-29: Intro call w/ Jordan (AE) — product overview, asked about dedicated sizing.
- 2026-02-10: Deep-dive demo + perf baseline (Fireflies ff_2026-02-10_aeq-dedicated-demo).
- 2026-02-18: POC agreement signed (NDA + sandbox access). SE Sofia ran initial perf sweep (see perf-results-2026-03-05.xlsx).
- 2026-03-05: Customer-run stress test in sandbox — sustained 42k tokens/sec observed with 10% variance; P99 token latency ~140ms (not meeting target).
- 2026-03-08: Joint architecture session — discussed reserve GPU counts, batching/kv-cache, and model routing fallback.
- 2026-03-09: Legal & procurement kick-off, sent draft MSA with standard Redwood SLA. Procurement pushed back on lack of hard tokens/sec term.

Action items / POC milestones:
- Redwood to provide a formal throughput guarantee proposal with measurement methodology by 2026-03-12. Include: how tokens/sec is measured (ingress vs emitted tokens), window sizes, and credit calculations.
- Run targeted perf pass with quantized model + recommended batching profile; target: sustained >=45k tokens/sec and P99 <=120ms. Deadline: 2026-03-20.
- Draft contract amendment language for min_tokens_per_second, burst_policy, and credit formula; collaborate with customer legal.
- Prepare an operational runbook: reserved GPU failover steps, autoscale thresholds, monitored metrics, and alerting channels.

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "If we don't get a contractual floor we can't move to prod — risk too high for trading-hours spikes."
- "We will accept temporary degraded quality in fallback model but not total timeouts for the user flow."

Negotiation nuances & traps:
- Customer expects hard numbers but Redwood's default is capacity-based billing with probabilistic performance guarantees; must translate to measurable tokens/sec terms without overcommitting.
- Need to negotiate burst metering: credit-based or time-windowed throttles. They prefer short over-age forgiveness rather than immediate throttling.
- Legal wants an auditor clause for on-prem deployments (reporting + access during incidents). Procurement flagged data-residency language for EU customers.

Next steps (concise):
- Deliver throughput proposal + measurement plan (Jordan/Sofia).
- SE-run perf with revised batching + quantization (Sofia).
- Legal redline MSA draft (Jordan + Redwood legal) and review with Aequitas legal 2026-03-18.
